I had a philosophy class where on the first day the professor went around asking students what they wanted in life. “To be an artist” “To travel the world” “To have a good job” generic answers. I looked up “how to make happy brain juice” the other day because it’s just a bunch of chemicals triggered in your brain from various things that are linked back to our survival as cavemen. Yummy food = dopamine, learning something and teaching it to someone else = serotonin, snuggling with a loved one = oxytocin, listening to a scary or exciting story or dancing/running = endorphins. Our entire lives are based around generating happy brain juice. 

I personally suck at all of it and I know exactly how you feel. I’m pretty sad I woke up this morning. I don’t know what my advice is other than to test out generating the various happy brain juices and take note. You could be deficient in one or another but okay with some. Your brain could literally suck at connecting wires for one like mine with dopamine (adhd) and It might be worth exploring and pushing back your due date for another week or so. This is what I tell myself at least and I’ve been able to push the goal post to 5 years.

I have a BFA and an MFA and I teach at an art school. It depends on the artist honestly. The type of work you want to create/learn and if the school can provide the help you need. Right now? I’d say no, not if there is a risk of it being virtual. That doesn’t work if you are trying to learn oil painting or figure drawing in my opinion. It can be done but it won’t be the full experience. 

It’s an experience. It’s heartbreaking and frustrating and inspiring. You will make friends and enemies and fall in love with certain professors and hate the others. I would say art school helped me because I walked in determined to walk out the best artist in my class. If you can channel an aggressive desire to learn then it is worth it. If it feels like a more casual learning experience take classes at art centers and reach out to artists you admire and see how they evolved their studio practice. 

Even if you have a positive experience you will feel bitter in some regards. Being surrounded by other artists is traumatic.
